definition: 2,3-Bisphosphoglycerate; erythrocyte glycolytic metabolite that binds deoxyhemoglobin to shift the O2 dissociation curve rightward, facilitating tissue oxygen release.
True increase in total circulating red blood cell mass (>25% above normal), subdivided into primary and secondary causes.
Abnormal variation in the size of red blood cells, quantified by the Red Cell Distribution Width (RDW).
Intractable burning itching without cutaneous lesions provoked by warm water contact; pathognomonic clinical feature of Polycythemia Vera.
Precipitated ribosomal RNA distributed throughout the erythrocyte, seen in lead poisoning, thalassemia, and sideroblastic anemia.
Erythrocytes with semicircular peripheral defect created when splenic macrophages pluck out Heinz bodies in G6PD deficiency.
Occlusion of hepatic venous outflow causing hepatomegaly, ascites, and abdominal pain; frequently caused by latent Polycythemia Vera.
Erythrocytes with regularly spaced, blunt spicules across the membrane; classically seen in uremia, renal failure, and liver dysfunction.
Hemoglobin complexed with carbon monoxide; unable to bind oxygen and shifts remaining tetramers left, causing smoker's polycythemia.
Colony-Forming Unit-Erythroid; late erythroid bone marrow progenitor possessing high densities of functional erythropoietin receptors.
Direct Antiglobulin Test; detects antibodies (IgG) or complement (C3d) bound directly to the patient's red blood cell membrane.
Glycoprotein hormone synthesized by renal cortical interstitial fibroblasts in response to low PO2, driving erythroid survival and proliferation.
Episodic burning pain, warmth, and erythema of the hands/feet due to platelet microthrombosis in polycythemia vera; dramatically relieved by aspirin.
Destruction of abnormal or antibody-coated red blood cells by macrophages within the splenic red pulp cords and hepatic Kupffer cells.
Major intracellular iron storage protein complex; serum ferritin is the most sensitive non-invasive indicator of total body iron stores.
The only identified cellular iron export channel in enterocytes and macrophages; targeted for degradation by hepcidin.
Relative or stress erythrocytosis characterized by elevated hematocrit due to reduced plasma volume in hypertensive, obese males.
Serum alpha-2 glycoprotein that binds free hemoglobin dimers with high affinity; levels drop to near zero during intravascular hemolysis.
Insoluble clumps of oxidized, denatured hemoglobin visualized on supravital stains in G6PD deficiency and unstable hemoglobinopathies.
Volume percentage of whole blood composed of packed red blood cells; normal is ~40-52% in adult males and ~36-48% in adult females.
Insoluble granular iron storage complex visualized with Prussian blue stain; shed into urine during intravascular hemolysis.
Hepatic peptide hormone induced by IL-6 that binds and internalizes ferroportin, causing systemic iron trapping in Anemia of Chronic Disease.
Hypoxia-Inducible Factor 1-alpha; master transcription factor degraded in normoxia by prolyl hydroxylases but stabilized in hypoxia to drive EPO gene transcription.
Neutrophils exhibiting 6 or more nuclear lobes (or >5% with 5 lobes); pathognomonic peripheral blood finding of megaloblastic anemia.
Decreased hemoglobin content inside erythrocytes, causing an expanded central pale area (>1/3 of diameter) and reduced MCHC.
Lysis of red blood cells within the circulation, releasing free hemoglobin into plasma, depleting haptoglobin, and causing hemoglobinuria.
Somatic gain-of-function valine-to-phenylalanine mutation at codon 617 of Janus Kinase 2, present in >95% of Polycythemia Vera cases.
Concave, spoon-shaped malformation of fingernails classically seen in longstanding, severe iron deficiency anemia.
Abnormally enlarged red blood cells with Mean Corpuscular Volume (MCV) exceeding 100 fL.
Average volume of a single erythrocyte in femtoliters (fL). Normal reference range: 80 to 100 fL.
Giant, abnormal erythroid precursor in bone marrow demonstrating nuclear-cytoplasmic dyssynchrony caused by defective DNA synthesis.
Ratio of MCV to RBC count (millions). Value < 13 suggests Thalassemia trait; > 13 suggests Iron Deficiency Anemia.
Abnormally small erythrocytes with Mean Corpuscular Volume (MCV) below 80 fL.
Simultaneous hypercellular proliferation of all three hematopoietic bone marrow lineages: erythroid, granulocytic, and megakaryocytic.
Autoimmune gastritis with destruction of gastric parietal cells, causing intrinsic factor deficiency and severe Vitamin B12 malabsorption.
Ruddy, dusky reddish-purple skin and mucous membrane discoloration caused by engorgement of capillaries with packed red cells.
Presence of abnormally shaped red blood cells (e.g., target cells, sickle cells, spherocytes, schistocytes) on blood smear.
Clonal myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by autonomous trilineage marrow proliferation driven by JAK2 mutation and suppressed EPO.
Apparent elevation in hematocrit and Hb caused by reduced intravascular plasma volume with normal true total red cell mass.
Young, non-nucleated erythrocyte containing residual ribosomal RNA; serves as the primary clinical gauge of marrow erythropoietic response.
Calculated value correcting reticulocyte percentage for both anemia severity and premature marrow shift; RPI > 2 indicates adequate marrow response.
Fragmented red blood cell (helmet cell) formed by mechanical shearing against intravascular fibrin strands in microangiopathic hemolytic anemias.
Erythroblast containing iron granules in cytoplasm; ringed sideroblasts feature iron accumulation in perinuclear mitochondria.
Demyelination of spinal cord dorsal and lateral columns caused by B12 deficiency; presents with sensory ataxia and spastic weakness.
Erythrocytes with central hemoglobin collection surrounded by clear ring and outer rim; seen in thalassemia, hemoglobin C, and liver disease.
Laboratory measure of maximum iron that transferrin can bind; elevated in iron deficiency, decreased in anemia of chronic disease.
